title: unified-rollouts-probing-quarantine-autorollback-workflow-improvements
author: Priya Patel
description: Motivation: Reduce noisy/false-positive autorollbacks by adding a lightweight probing stage plus quarantine window before triggering full rollback. This change implements a probing+quarantine stage in the unified rollout controller so that small transient metric spikes don't immediately rollback canaries or shadow experiments. It also improves observability and tracing to make automated decisions auditable. Summary of changes: add `probing` stage to rollout state machine, implement `quarantine` tracking and cooldown windows, wire probing decisions into the autorollback engine, expose new metrics and traces for probing/quarantine decisions, add canary/AB/shadow integration tests and e2e scenarios, update docs and examples. Checklist: - [x] Add probing stage and quarantine policy implementation in rollout controller - [x] Integrate probing output into autorollback coordinator - [x] Emit telemetry (rollout.probe.* metrics, rollout.quarantine.* tags) - [x] Add unit tests for state transitions and edge cases - [x] Add e2e tests that simulate transient spikes and persistent degradations - [x] Update rollout docs and changelog - [x] Run perf suite to ensure no regression Context: Previous autorollback behavior used immediate metric threshold triggers which caused several false rollbacks during transient infra noise (see linked Linear ENG-2314). The new probing stage performs short-duration probes (configurable, default 30s) where additional requests are shadowed/probed, and quarantine maintains a short cooldown (configurable, default 5m) during which further automated rollback will be suppressed unless multiple independent probe failures occur. Observability: new metrics (rollout_probe_success_rate, rollout_probe_latency_p50/p90, rollout_quarantine_count) and tracing spans (rollout.probe.{start,decision}) are emitted; these are plumbed to the console dashboards. Testing: added comprehensive unit tests for the state machine and a pair of e2e scenarios: (1) transient spike that should be quarantined and recovered without rollback, (2) sustained degradation that triggers probe failure and then a rollback. Deployment notes: feature guarded behind a rollout config flag (`enable_probing_quarantine`) and respects existing rollout SLO/matching rules. Opt-in in Dedicated/Private through config overrides. See release notes for rollout default changes and backward compatibility notes.

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Overall approach looks good. Question: how do we avoid adding latency to normal canary paths?
Priya Patel: We run probes asynchronously and only shadow a small percentage of traffic during probe windows; normal path is unchanged unless probe fails.
Marta Ruiz: Suggest adding a safety to require 2 independent probe failures OR sustained metric breach for rollback. Can we make that configurable?
Priya Patel: Yes, added `failure_quorum` config and default is 1 but recommended set to 2 for noisy workloads. Documented in docs/rollouts/probing-quarantine.md.
Ethan Zhao: CI flake on e2e (timing) — adjusted probe timing in tests and added retries. Verified green in latest run.
Marta Ruiz: Approved after addressing config and docs. +1 from Liam. Merging once CI passes.
CI: pipeline succeeded, all checks green.
release_notes: Add probing and quarantine stages to unified rollouts: new configurable probe stage reduces false-positive autorollbacks by validating transient metric spikes before triggering rollback; adds new telemetry (rollout_probe_*/rollout_quarantine_*), e2e tests, and rollout config flag `enable_probing_quarantine` (default off for safe rollout).
